Source and root cause. On the malformed padded `NFULA_PREFIX` TLV, this line materializes the raw `recordLen` 5 instead of the required aligned size 8, so every later traversal step reasons about the wrong TLV extent.

The reader uses the step-1 size `5` in both its bounds check and its pointer arithmetic. For the padded `NFULA_PREFIX` record that means the next-record cursor is placed three bytes early, inside the prefix padding rather than at the real 4-byte-aligned next TLV boundary.

Because step 2 landed in zero padding, `assign()` skips those padding bytes and reanchors `m_Data` on the next nonzero bytes. The parser now treats later bytes as if they started a fresh TLV header instead of recognizing that traversal had already gone out of sync.

After step 3 hides the alignment gap, the search can continue through later bytes and still return a non-null record for `recordType == 9` (`NFULA_PAYLOAD`). That record becomes the authoritative payload descriptor for the rest of parsing.

The returned `NFULA_PAYLOAD` record is trusted as authoritative. `parseNextLayer()` converts its header into a payload pointer and a claimed `payloadLen` without checking that the value still fits inside the real packet buffer; the saved ASan allocation context shows the backing packet allocation is only 28 bytes.

anchors.note: This validator checks only the claimed `payloadLen` and the first IPv4 header nibble/IHL fields at `payload`. It does not verify that the underlying packet allocation actually contains a full IPv4 header and destination-address field.
Because step 6 accepts the shifted, overclaimed payload as IPv4, `parseNextLayer()` instantiates an `IPv4Layer` over those bytes instead of falling back to `PayloadLayer`.

On the next parse-loop iteration `curLayer` is the IPv4Layer from step 7, so Packet records the packet as `IPv4` in `m_ProtocolTypes`. This is the exact state the harness queries before calling the IPv4 address getters.
Because step 8 set the IPv4 protocol bit, the fuzz target enters its IPv4-only branch and immediately reads the source and destination addresses from the parsed IPv4 layer.

Sink. The harness retrieves the IPv4Layer created in step 7 and this getter reads the 4-byte destination-address field from its backing bytes. ASan reports that read exactly at the end of the 28-byte heap region allocated for the raw packet in `pcpp::PcapFileReaderDevice::getNextPacket()`.

Root cause. NFLOG TLV size is taken verbatim from `recordLen` instead of being aligned to 4 bytes, so a padded `NFULA_PREFIX` record contributes 5 bytes instead of its real 8-byte footprint. That under-advance is what lets later traversal step into padding and reinterpret later bytes as another TLV.
ASan crash site. Once the malformed NFLOG payload has been accepted as IPv4, this getter reads the 4-byte destination-address field from an IPv4Layer backed by a too-short heap packet buffer.
